newsitem.title: UK: Iraqi absence cuts June OPEC output to 26.39 mbpd.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi absence cuts June OPEC output to 26.39 mbpd.

text.p: OPEC output in June fell for the second month in succession, but not because of any voluntary restraint among those in the cartel who are pumping more than officially mandated quotas.
Delays in the resumption of Iraqi exports under the United Nations' humanitarian oil deal were behind the lower OPEC output.

Wellhead June crude output in June from the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries fell 430,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 26.39 million from a revised 26.82 million in May, a Reuters survey found.
Iraqi sales under the first six-month phase of the agreement ended at the end of May and are expected to restart some time between mid-July and early August.
For Iraq to meet its permitted $2 billion target by early December, its exports over four months would have to run at about one million bpd, putting OPEC well above 27 million bpd.
Iraq's absence from the market knocked some 730,000 bpd out of the OPEC equation for June but extra oil from the rest of the group made up for almost half of the Iraqi shortfall.
Baghdad pumped 670,000 bpd for domestic consumption, compared to 1.40 million in May.
New supplies were added in June by Venezuela and Nigeria, OPEC's leading quota violators, while Iran and the United Arab Emirates both resumed normal flows after maintenance in May.

Venezuela, the centre of attention at last week's OPEC meeting in Vienna, was put at 3.15 million bpd in June after some small downward revisions to previous estimates for earlier in the year. Its quota is 2.359 million bpd.

Caracas, having averaged 3.07 million bpd for the first quarter and 3.14 million for the second, would have to accelerate production increases to reach state oil company PDVSA's 3.245 million target for the year.
Although Iran and Saudi Arabia joined forces at OPEC in an effort to stem quota-busting, chances of Venezuela reversing its expanded production policy now are deemed negligible.
OPEC ended the Vienna talks with an extension of its 25.03 million bpd ceiling until the end of the year and renewed vows to stick to quotas.
But alleged violators, including Nigeria and Venezuela, immediately devalued the deal by reiterating public denials of overproduction.
Monitors said Iran, lacking the capacity to produce much beyond its quota, dragged output back to 3.63 million bpd in June after maintenance hit flows in May.
The UAE also recovered most, though not all, of May maintenance reductions.
A trouble-free month in Nigeria allowed supplies to rise to 2.23 million bpd, excluding condensates not spiked into crude shipments.
New drilling and production technologies have allowed Nigeria's joint venture partners to raise flows despite budget restrictions.
Saudi Arabia was running at a consistent 8.10 million, not including some 150,000 bpd of Saudi crude given to non-OPEC Gulf neighbour Bahrain which Riyadh considers outside its OPEC quota.
The Reuter survey seeks a best estimate of wellhead flows in OPEC countries based on the views of officials, industry monitors and analysts inside and outside member countries.
OPEC quotas are based on supply to market, defined to exclude movements to, but not sales from storage.
